title: Turkey ratifies mutual-defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia
dek: An attack on one is to be treated as an attack on all three. India has said it is studying what the Mecca agreement means for its security.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Turkey's parliament on Thursday ratified the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, a pact under which an armed attack on any one of the three countries is treated as an attack on all of them. The bill passed by 279 votes to 119, Türkiye Today reported, and the state-run Anadolu Agency said the vote clears the way for the agreement to take effect.

The ratification makes Turkey's commitment to the pact legally binding at home at a time when Saudi Arabia is fighting Yemen's Houthis, who have fired missiles and drones at Saudi cities, airports and oil sites. Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have reportedly already completed their own ratification, according to Türkiye Today.

## What the agreement says

The 16-article agreement was signed on 7 August by Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, The Wire reported. Besides the mutual-defence clause, it covers counter-terrorism, intelligence sharing, joint exercises, defence-industry cooperation and logistics, according to Türkiye Today.

The Turkish bill has three articles: it approves the agreement, says it enters into force on publication in Turkey's Official Gazette, and gives the president responsibility for carrying it out. The agreement itself takes effect once all three countries deposit their ratification documents with its secretariat in Saudi Arabia, Türkiye Today reported. A retired Pakistani lieutenant general, Nauman Mahmood, has been appointed the first secretary-general of the pact's joint committee.

The mutual-defence clause does not send troops automatically. Help is given to an attacked member only if it asks, and the three decide its nature and scope by consensus, according to Türkiye Today. Any deployment of Turkish troops abroad needs a separate vote in parliament, and new members need the unanimous consent of the three founders. The pact has no end date, and members cannot withdraw for the first ten years.

A ruling-party lawmaker told Reuters that Turkey would also submit a mandate allowing military personnel to be deployed to Saudi Arabia under the pact, The Jerusalem Post reported. Turkish officials have said the agreement is defensive and that no Turkish troops would be sent to fight in Yemen.

## What they are saying

Ziya Altunyaldiz, a lawmaker from President Erdogan's AK Party, told parliament the agreement contained no approach directed against any third country and that its main goal was to "prevent conflicts rather than escalate them", Anadolu reported. Mehmet Guzelmansur of the main opposition CHP said clear rules were needed so that the pact did not contradict Turkey's other international obligations. Opposition parties argued during the debate that the agreement could pull Turkey into regional wars.

Syria's foreign minister, Asaad al-Shaibani, said on Saturday that "discussions are currently underway" on Syria joining, The Jerusalem Post reported. Saudi Arabia and Syria signed a separate military cooperation agreement on Wednesday, the details of which have not been made public.

## Why it matters for India

The pact binds Pakistan to two of the most influential states in the Muslim world, one of which, Saudi Arabia, India describes as a strategic partner. It builds on the bilateral Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement that Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed in September 2025.

India has not objected to the pact. When it was signed, the External Affairs Ministry's spokesperson, Randhir Jaiswal, said at his weekly briefing on 11 August that India was "examining its implications both from the perspective of our national security" and regional stability, and that "India remains fully committed to meeting or safeguarding its national interest", The Wire reported. After the 2025 Saudi-Pakistan agreement, he said India expected its strategic partnership with Riyadh to "keep in mind mutual interests and sensitivities", The Tribune reported.

Saudi Arabia has said the arrangement is not a military alliance or a religious bloc and does not involve nuclear pursuits, according to The Tribune.

## What happens next

The agreement will enter into force once the ratification documents are deposited in Saudi Arabia. Any decision to send Turkish forces to Saudi Arabia would need a separate parliamentary mandate in Ankara. Whether Syria, and possibly Qatar, join will show whether the pact grows beyond its three founders.
